txt: Breathing on the other end suggests that Sylvie is still on the line. She heard everything.
Her voice reappears from the static: "That's wonderful, really. Maybe you should keep pursuing that hobby. Maybe it would calm you down a little."
There is silence on the other end of the line.
There's a pause. You can almost see her on the other side, the telephone cord coiled around her index.
There's no reply from the other end of the line.
You can almost hear the girl getting smaller on the other end of the line, until she almost drowns in static.
You hear a sigh of relief on the other end of the radio. Wordless, the call breaks. Then the already familiar voice:
You hear static. Her chin rub against the receiver. Then: "Please, I just didn't want any trouble."
You hear the call breaking up on the other end of the radio and then the already familiar voice:
"'We Go On' by the OO." She sighs. "I can't listen to it anymore, you've turned it into a parody."
"*Please* don't bring Garte into this, it's none of your business!"
"All sorts of things. The OO. Some disco, rock too. So much disco and rock..."
"And *then* I had to deal with your toilet. The one you clogged with *police documents*, causing water damage downstairs in the kitchen."
"And then you screamed something incomprehensible about churches and the scent of apricots and aquariums." She takes a deep breath.
"Didn't seem like you had fun doing it though."
"Especially when there's a hurricane loose. It's *your* fault for losing them -- not mine."
"Especially when there's a hurricane loose. It's your fault for losing them -- not mine."
"Even about little things, like not turning down the volume at 3 AM. I even *liked* one of those songs you kept listening to on repeat. No more. I hate it now."
"God, I... I knew I shouldn't have brought it up. Just... try not to call me again and let's pretend it never happened."
"Good. Then it's not lost." She seems a little relieved. "Just don't throw it in the toilet again. Toilets don't work like that."
"Great." There's relief in her voice. "Anything else?"
"I *really* don't want to talk about this. Let's just forget about this, okay?"
"I already said I don't want to talk about this! You're messing everything up again!"
"I am sorry about that." She doesn't sound like she's actually that sorry. "Anything else, detective?"
"I bet."
"I didn't know *what* to say to him later. Then you came and destroyed the place. So I left without explaining. I should have told him maybe..."
"I do hope so. Please don't call me again. Bye." She's ready to hang up.
"I don't know what to tell you, officer. I didn't call you, because I didn't want to get in trouble with the others, with the Union. I'm sorry about that."
"I think you said it had been *giving you shit ever since you got there*."
"I tried to send the cleaner, but you wouldn't let me. Threatened to 'make me understand'. I had no idea what you meant -- and I *don't* want to know."
"I won't even *mention* you waving your gun around, harassing customers, *threatening* to sing karaoke, threatening to kill yourself..."
"I'm not mad, it's just..." The static sighs again. "You were so drunk and so emotional all the time, and then the *skua thing* happened. It just made me want to quit."
"I've had sailors fighting, Union guys grabbing my ass, kids stealing booze. Once a guy was glued to the karaoke machine every night for two months. But *you*..." She pauses.
"I, ugh... the ones I had to wrench out of your toilet."
"I, ugh... the ones I had to wrench out of your toilet?"
"I, uh..." The static wavers. "Let's just say I left because I needed to get away from someone."
"I... I didn't know I had to report it... I... I thought someone would take him down eventually..." Her voice breaks.
"I... I didn't want to get in trouble with the others..."
"I... dammit, I don't remember what I did to your damn papers! I don't remember every little thing I do..." Resentment gives way to concern in her voice.
"I... dammit, I don't remember what I did to your damn papers! I don't remember every little thing I do." Resentment gives way to concern in her voice.
"It almost looked like you pawned it, but believe me, I did *not* ask." She sighs.
"It was a pretty bird, there since I started working in the Whirling. I really liked her. We called her Scotty..."
"Maybe, I don't know..." She seems to relax a little bit. "I just know I have to take some time off right now."
"Me neither."
"Mhmh."
"No idea. All I know is, next you were waving around money instead. Saying things like 'Big bucks cannot lie' and 'Guns can't buy money, but money can always buy guns'."
"No one calls the police." You can hear her adjust the receiver in her hand. "The Union would get angry."
"No, I don't know. It wasn't me..." She gulps. "I haven't been out there since... I was terrified of the stench and the corpse." She falls silent.
"No, I was actually flattered, I've always liked him. It was just bad timing... with the corpse and all that."
"No, absolutely not."
"No, not me."
"No, please, no more suicide threats! Thank *god* you don't have that stupid gun anymore..."
"No, sorry... I don't." She clears her throat. "Not a lot of people have phones around here. Copper thieves take the wires..."
"No, you really weren't. You were simply the worst."
"No. What?"
"No..." You can hear her regaining control in the background. "I honestly don't know."
"Oh god." The static appears to breathe heavily. "Please just stay out of my li..."
"Oh, all sorts of things. Some disco, rock too. So much disco and rock..."
"Oh, great." She doesn't sound thrilled. "What else do you need, detective?"
"Oh, right..." She recognizes your voice almost immediately. "Hello, officer, what can I do for you?"
"Oh... no, I haven't, sorry."
"Okay, but... please don't mess it up. Please don't take out your gun or something."
"Okay, officer..." Her voice is withdrawing as if she's moving away from the speaker.
"Okay..." She's calmer now. Probably because the focus has shifted elsewhere.
"Okay." She obviously doesn't want to challenge your authority. You feel *much* better now.
"People don't have the money to have the cables put in again. They use the Union's phone or the one on the coast."
"Please, no. Not this again -- everyone saw your 'cool gun', detective..." She sounds beyond exacerbated.
"Right. Well... Are we almost done now, officer?"
"Sad? I think the one you mean is "The Smallest Church in Saint-Saëns". Butchered that right up..." Her voice carries a tone of disappointment.
"Sorry about that." She doesn't sound like she's too sorry. "Anything else, detective?"
"The other people who live around here. Local people. I... I didn't want trouble... "
"The stuffed bird. The great skua. You threw it against the wall, while screaming 'fuck that bird' and laughing like a maniac."
"Then there was your room. Your *project*, an experiment to see how bad it can get in there."
"To hell with that song..."
"Uniform? I never saw you in any uniform, you had your... *things* on. The disco things."
"Wait, really? No, this is absolutely not true. I like Garte, I really do."
"Well... You were worse than all of them. Honestly, you were getting borderline aggressive."

"Well." There's an uncomfortable pause. "You tried to jam it down the toilet, sir, clogging it completely. After I had *unclogged* the toilet and retrieved the paperwork I threw it out in the trash, thinking you didn't need it."
"What? Of course it bothered me! But I thought the Union already knew about the corpse."
"What?" She stops abruptly. "No, why would you even think that?!"
"Which one would that be?"
"Yeah, go on."
"Yes, I know who you are. You're a police officer... *the law*."
"Yes, I'm sure. Every time we talk about it I'm going to be *more* sure I don't know."
"Yes, hello!" A female voice greets you through static -- it sounds like she's million miles away from here.
"Yes, hello." You recognize her voice.
"Yes, obviously. You were the worst client I've ever seen. And I have seen *so many* assholes in this place..."
"Yes, well..." The static on the radio suggests Sylvie doesn't have a comment.
"Yes. That's the one you liked to sing along to the *most*. The later it got the more *that one* came on."
"Yes. You put *something* there. Causing bad water damage in the kitchen. I think it was that."
"Yes... I know, it's just..." She takes a deep breath before continuing. "Was there anything else?"
"You do?" She sounds relieved. "What else can I do for you?"
"You don't live here, you *don't* understand. Squealing is frowned upon here -- everything is dealt with... well, by the Union. Internally."
"You have to ask someone else. There are thousands of people in Martinaise."
"You know whom."
"You know..." She seems to be looking for words. "What the Union says, goes. People listen to them and they take care of their own, which is, like, everyone here."
"You mean why did I leave the bar?" You can hear her tense up on the other side. "Honestly, I'm... not really comfortable discussing it with you, sir."
"You told me back in the Whirling... you told *everybody*. And showed us your badge... I don't need to hear about it anymore."
"You were trying to *impress* some people with it. Everyone was eating and..." She stops hesitantly, not sure if she should continue.
"You were waving it around in everyone's face, begging them to describe it. You said it 'calms you'. And then you started making suicide jokes. It got pretty *graphic*."
